subject: Scope confirmation & decision checklist for internal advocate
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: scope & decision criteria (next steps)

Liam — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the asks I promised:  

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + agent assist for scale (priority: reduce handle time, cut external call transfers).
- Success metrics: 40% reduction in average handle time (AHT) for tier-1, maintain NPS within ±2 points.
- Data sensitivity: PII in transcripts; security/legal flagged SOC 2 and retention controls as gating items.

Key clarifying questions / asks for you:
1) Economic buyer: who signs on budget? You mentioned a VP of Product — can you confirm name/role?
2) Procurement & legal: please share the procurement contact and legal security lead so we can route the SOC2 + data flow docs.
3) Decision criteria: beyond latency/cost, are there hard constraints (on-prem requirement, encryption-at-rest, data residency)?

Proposed next steps (I suggest):
- We prepare a 1-page ROI summary for the economic buyer (Sara McBride?) and a short security one-pager for legal.
- Schedule a 30–45m technical touchpoint with your security/infra and our SEs (we can do the week of Apr 25).
- Share a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones: pilot scope, procurement review, legal review, pilot start.

Attachments: initial-sow-outline.pdf (attachment stub) — lightweight scope draft.

If you can confirm procurement contact + economic buyer by EOD Tuesday, we'll have the 1-pagers to you within 48 hours.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintechlabs.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Fintech Labs Procurement <procurement@fintechlabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: scope & decision criteria (next steps)

Michael — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers:  

- Economic buyer: Sara McBride, Head of Data (cc'd here — sara.mcbride@fintechlabs.com). She's the primary budget owner for platform work.
- Procurement: procurement@fintechlabs.com is the right inbox to start intake. They'll loop in our vendor security team.
- Legal/security asks: vendor SOC 2 Type II report, encryption-at-rest, and a short data retention & deletion policy are required. No on-prem requirement at this stage, but data residency in the US is preferred.

Timeline: procurement kick-off week of Apr 25, but Sara wants a high-level cost/ROI and MAP before the kickoff so she can brief the execs. If you can share an ROI 1-pager and the MAP by Apr 22 that'd be ideal.

I can coordinate a 30-min joint call with procurement + security on Apr 26 — will confirm availability.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Principal Product Manager, Integrations
Fintech Labs
liam.oconnor@fintechlabs.com

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 09:12 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Liam — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the asks I promised: ...

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: scope & decision criteria — internal advocate brief (please review)

Team — forwarding Liam's reply and procurement window. Quick internal brief and asks for prep before Apr 22 deliverable.

Context (from discovery): Fintech Labs wants to reduce AHT for tier-1 support and keep NPS stable. Economic buyer is Sara McBride (Head of Data); procurement kickoff expected week of Apr 25. Legal/security will require SOC2, encryption-at-rest, and a retention policy.

What I need from you by EOD Apr 21:
- Priyom: suggested MAP with milestones and low/high-level durations (pilot start date, legal review, procurement sign-off). Keep it one slide/one doc.
- Neha: security one-pager: bullets covering SOC2 posture, encryption, data access & deletion process, and recommended next steps for their security team.
- Ben: ROI 1-pager for Sara (seller-facing talk track + top-line numbers). We should include: estimated token cost per conversation, projected AHT improvement lift scenarios (20/40/60%), and an intro to Redwood Dedicated options for predictable throughput.

Talk tracks and framing suggestions (for the advocate to use with Sara):
- Business: pilot focused on high-volume agent queue to prove AHT reduction; low risk because transcripts only (no PII extraction in pilot).
- Economic: present conservative (20%) and target (40%) AHT reductions with estimated labor savings and break-even months.
- Security: proactively provide SOC2 evidence and a clear data retention/deletion SLA to shorten legal review.

Attachments: advocate-one-pager-draft.docx (drafts we can iterate on).

I'll run these materials by Liam as soon as we have them; objective is to have Sara briefed prior to the procurement kickoff.

Best,
Michael

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: scope & decision criteria — internal advocate brief (please review)

Looping in to confirm next steps — I'll take the ROI 1-pager and will run numbers with SE. Quick notes:  

- I'll draft a one-page with three scenarios (conservative/expected/aggressive) and include a unit-cost sensitivity for token pricing vs expected monthly volume.
- SE can join the Apr 26 procurement/security call — I'll ask for availability and include an estimated time commitment.
- Attached pricing-sketch.xlsx (attachment stub) with preliminary figures — please do not share externally yet; it's internal draft.

Will have first pass to you both by Apr 21 EOD.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
